reviewed_question_hash_basis: SHA256 of each raw author question serialized as UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, ensure_ascii=false and compact comma/colon separators; these hashes are distinct from generated public question content hashes.
review_method: Read every final English scenario, lead-in and option and every Korean option rationale in the four retained new questions. Separately read both existing quality questions proposed for reuse and all six assigned original representatives.

Read current official-URL text for 247 CMR 8 and Policy 2020-15 through a fresh peer Exa request; read the relevant 247 CMR 9 paragraphs in the official-URL extraction already retrieved for this team's source research. Cross-check the CII inventory and current policy clauses through system1 official search excerpts.

Directly open and read eCFR 21 CFR 1306.25, relevant Schedule II entries in 1308.12, and the NABP current competency page. Retrieve 105 CMR 721 official-URL full text separately and cross-check its Schedule VI oral-format exception with the official indexed passage.

Compare the retained cases with related questions in the unchanged prior96, prior46 and canonical corpus. Record constituent-rule overlap without claiming that all four questions add wholly new law or that the entire corpus is semantically unique.

Check final source-reference resolution, note-unit resolution, per-option character/word lengths, keys, pre-2027 outline boundary and the two reserved-ID reuse decisions. Do not modify the authoring file or the reused question files.

choice_review.A: False. Ordinary-technician unchanged-refill limits are not the full scope of a currently licensed nationally certified technician; the stated VI oral format is permitted.
choice_review.B: True. Title identification, current credentials and pharmacist approval support receiving the prescriber-defined new information, followed by pharmacist review.
choice_review.C: False. The permitted receipt does not authorize final dispensing validation.
choice_review.D: False. Required fields being present does not authorize technician DUR or clinical review.

Canonical MA-Q-0234 and MA-Q-0411 already contain the same underlying new/omitted-information rule, so this is not counted as a globally new legal principle.

choice_review.A: False. A later pharmacist signature does not make the actual transfer communication pharmacist-to-pharmacist.
choice_review.B: False. Prior dispensing identifies the refill-transfer pathway, whose direct pharmacist-communication requirement remains.
choice_review.C: False. Valid facility DEA registrations do not expand the technician's VI-only transfer permission.
choice_review.D: True. Direct communication between the two licensed pharmacists is the applicable pathway for the otherwise eligible IV refill transfer.

Canonical MA-Q-0235 already states the VI-only technician boundary and MA-Q-0120 applies it to an eligible VI transfer. The new case applies the IV pharmacist handoff in the improved default representative pool; it is not a new law in the entire corpus.
questions.length_review: Choice character counts A96/B101/C93/D86. The correct assignment is shorter than each distractor; its validity follows the communication rule rather than accumulated detail.

choice_review.A: True. The ordinary technician may stay within approved completed-prescription transport while the pharmacist performs raw-stock counting.
choice_review.B: False. Later pharmacist final verification does not authorize an otherwise excluded staff handling task.
choice_review.C: False. Amending an internal transport procedure cannot confer certified-technician handling authority.
choice_review.D: False. Combining two ordinary technicians does not confer the separate nationally certified-technician permissions.

questions.scenario_and_key: Opening the methylphenidate stock bottle and counting a new prescription is a concrete handling assignment, unlike the already verified package transport. The formulation is not the narrowly excluded hydrocodone-only ER category; the question does not infer current product availability.

Canonical MA-Q-0076 contains the same underlying ordinary-versus-certified CII transport/handling rule. This case improves the practical assignment decision for the original representative and does not claim a globally new rule.
questions.length_review: Choice character counts A75/B72/C78/D68. Choices are short parallel assignment plans; A is not the longest by characters.

choice_review.A: False. Two technicians' signatures do not replace the supervising pharmacist's verification that the count complied with Board requirements.
choice_review.B: True. The two-currently-certified-technician count pathway retains supervising pharmacist verification.
choice_review.C: False. Permission to make routine entries does not authorize a discrepancy adjustment, including the confirmed duplicate-entry adjustment here.
choice_review.D: False. The absent-MOR pharmacist-designee exception means the MOR's physical return is not a prerequisite. No immediate-adjustment deadline is asserted.
choice_review.E: True. The named pharmacist designee may adjust during the MOR's absence and must report the change to the MOR.

questions.scenario_and_key: The MOR's absence, explicit pharmacist designation, two current CPhTs and documented cause provide the conditions used by the key. The case preserves pharmacist verification and does not claim a conclusion about significant-loss or theft reporting.
questions.semantic_review: MA-REV-0017 has the MOR present and an unexplained shortage. Here absence and an explicit pharmacist designation change the authorized adjustment actor; the original PER14 rule is applied in a coherent count-and-correction scenario.
questions.length_review: Choice character counts A106/B106/C96/D72/E94. B ties a false option for longest; E is shorter. Two true choices out of five avoid the old all-correct pattern. Choice D was clarified without adding legal requirements.

choice_review.A: An ordinary technician's approved unchanged-refill role does not include the dose/directions change; pharmacist assessment is an appropriate next step.
choice_review.B: Unchanged ingredient and strength do not make changed directions an unchanged prescription.
choice_review.C: Insurance payment does not determine personnel scope.
choice_review.D: Relabeling the changed directions as a counseling note does not cure the unauthorized receipt.

choice_review.A: A second barcode scan is not a substitute for pharmacist final prescription verification.
choice_review.B: A second intern does not acquire pharmacist final-verification authority.

findings.finding: The former option D directed leaving the known duplicate until the MOR returned, while its rationale discussed whether waiting was mandatory. Because9.21(8)(d) permits a designee and does not itself state a new immediate-adjustment deadline, the option should test the mistaken actor restriction directly.
findings.resolution: The author changed D to treating the MOR's return as a prerequisite for any discrepancy adjustment and clarified its rationale. The peer reread the final option and exact regulatory paragraph; key BE is unchanged.

findings.finding: Canonical questions already contain the same lower-level technician receipt, transfer and handling rules. A new scenario in the representative collection must not be counted as a wholly new legal principle or proof of global semantic uniqueness.
findings.resolution: The root and author agreed to count these as improvements to existing representatives, outside the later120-gap-case goal. Same-rule canonical comparisons are recorded above; no canonical content or status was changed.

limitations: This is within-team peer review by another authoring agent, not an independent legal or realism audit under the repository's canonical release policy. It creates no LEGAL_VERIFICATION, REALISM_REVIEW or RELEASED record.

The reused questions were read for legal and decision-path fit, but their original source provenance and independent-review statuses remain unchanged. This report does not retrofit fresh source claims into their content.
No browser, persistence, scoring, deterministic-build or deployment checks were run as part of this question peer review. Those are separate root QA tasks.
